chunks: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding Maghrib: sometimes we pray while fearing that the sun may be behind the mountain, or that the mountain may have concealed it from us.
So he said to me: “You are not required to climb the mountain.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose setting marks the beginning of Maghrib time
key_terms.الْجَبَلِ: the mountain, which may obstruct direct sight of the sun
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the evening prayer at sunset

ai.seo_question: Are you required to climb a mountain to confirm sunset before praying Maghrib?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical ruling about the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) when mountains obstruct direct observation of the sun. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that one is not obligated to undertake unusual hardship, such as climbing a mountain, to verify sunset.
